content: This channel will become out way of getting how to use the bot and if we need help or have questions can ask here.  I will give V pin permission here if i can so he can pin important posts.

How I thought I'll do it for the initial infodump so you have something to check without having to wait for me is have messages that are kinda section separators and pin those so it'll be quicker to scroll through in the dropdown menu with pins, and then you can click them and go to the full text.

Most of the command info is in `?help` output (`?help command-name` for specific ones, as expected).
Commands for DMs are a bit more complex than the general ones, so while for the general commands you can get by with just `?help`, for DM commands `?help` won't contain everything for usability, and here will have more stuff like examples, and also stuff about the bot's automatic functions.
If something will need editing I'll edit it, otherwise I'll pin answers to any questions that might pop up
↓ What the bot does automatically ↓

- **scheduled messages**: main thing. The bot keeps messages to be sent once daily or once ever at specified times, to the specific channel.
- **clock**: at specified times (6 am, noon, 6 pm, 9 pm) there'll be a message in <#851552515345350657>, and messages older than 24h are deleted.
- **stocks**: every day at 6 am the bot will read new stock prices from Rob's spreadsheet
- **PC location tracking**: every time someone makes a message (except for OOC or any hidden channels), unless they're skipped from tracking (DMs and bots are), the bot takes note of the channel, so later anyone can check where someone was last. If someone was inactive for 24h they're removed from the list.
- **reactions**: if someone makes a message in a tracked channel, and it contains a specific word, the bot will add an emoji reaction to it
- **pins**: every time a message is pinned, that little "someone pinned a message to this channel" notification will be removed after 10 minutes
- **rollover**: every midnight the bot reloads its stuff, so errors don't accumulate. This does not take the bot offline.
- **automatic uptime**: if something in the code shits the bed and the bot goes down, it'll come back online within 5 minutes
↓ tl;dr of the commands all server members can use ↓

`?help`: displays command list with a tl;dr for each, `?help command-name` gives details for that command. Only commands you can use are visible and usable.

`?stocks`: lets players deal with stocks as set up by Rob, on its own the command lists prices, `?stocks mine` shows the player's portfolio, `?stocks buy` and `?stocks sell` do what they sound like

`?time`: displays current server time

`?where` shows which IC channel someone was last active, you can give it an @-mention, or a full display name, or the beginning of the display name (`?where roy` should match me now)

All commands are usable by private message to the bot, or in any channel in the server, but not in any other server.
↓ commands for DMs ↓

`?reaction` - adds an emoji reaction for the bot to use.
Called like `?reaction :fire_extinguisher: fireball`
will make it so if someone says "fireball" in an IC channel, the bot will add 🧯 as a reaction to the message

`?tasks`: shows if the automated tasks (not the act-on-a-message ones) are running right. It's ok if it says "running" for all of them, or "stopped" for "messages" task - that just means it ran out of messages for the day and will resume at midnight
`?stocks reload`: manually reload stock prices from Rob's spreadsheet. Normally shouldn't be needed, but just in case

`?message`: this is a big one. This command gives easier access to adding new scheduled messages to the bot, and is an extension of the file format I set up for holding those messages. The only thing about that format you need to worry about is how mentions are represented there, which is usable here too, which I'll describe in a bit.

Before I write any details, note that **this command has an interactive variant:** `?message interactive` (or just `?message i`), **which guides you through the process step-by-step**.
The only things you need to know for it is 1) that you can add a timeout in seconds (like `?message i 60` for 60 seconds) and that's how long the bot will wait for your response, default is 30. 2) how the plaintext mentions work if you don't want to ping people when setting the message up. If you plan to only use interactive, you can skip the rest of this message, and if you don't plan to use plaintext mentions, you can skip that one too.

To submit a message through the command, you call the command like this:
```
?message 2021-08-01 14:00 #new-player-landing
hello this is the start of the message content
all the stuff till the end of the message counts as text for the new message to schedule
that includes all the mentions that might be here, both normal ones and the plaintext ones
```
- timestamp: is `HH:MM` for daily messages, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` for one-time messages. Server time, 24h clock.
- channel: either channel name, or the clickable #-link to it
- message: obviously must be under character limit, but the header line will ensure that. Can have the normal, clickable, ping-making mentions, and can contain the plaintext mention placeholders as mentioned above, details about them in the next message.
↓ how the square brackets plaintext mentions work (completely optional) ↓

They look like this: `@[some stuff in square brackets]` and don't make the clickable pinging mentions, but let you do a fuzzy match.
That was needed for adding messages directly to files on Dropbox, but isn't required here. The biggest use cases are doing @[everyone] or if you don't want to ping fellow DMs while setting up the message.
Other than that, people *should not* get pinged by mentions in channels they can't access. At least our recent tests show that.

The way that works is by trying to match the stuff in square brackets to something - the first thing from this list is what gets used:
- if it's `@[everyone]`, it'll be converted into an everyone ping when the scheduled message is sent.
- role by role name
- player by their discord id (the long one)
- player by exact current displayed name, if they've been active in the last 24h
- player by their nickname otherwise, or by their account name, or account name with 4-digit discriminator (like Versil#6074), but not nickname + discriminator
- player by beginning part of their displayed name or account name, ignoring case (so for example @[ver] would match Versil)

So in a practical example:
- account name: `Versil`
- account discriminator: `6074`
- server nickname: `Roy | Versil (H)`
- account id: `148682928434577408`

All the following will work:
- account name, `@[Versil]`
- part of account name, even lowercase, `@[vers]`
- server nickname, `@[Roy | Versil (H)]`
- part of server nickname, even lowercase, `@[roy | versil]` or `@[roy]`
- account name + discriminator, `@[Versil#6074]`
- account id, `@[148682928434577408]`

This one **will definitely not work** (but is pointless as you shouldn't need the discriminator):
- server nickname + discriminator, `@[Roy | Versil (H)#6074]`

It might happen that the input can match multiple people - you might not get the right result then, and I can't guarantee it'd get the person you want - it won't do multiple at once.

`?here` - only usable in an IC channel (private messages not allowed either), lists everyone who was last active in the current channel. You can use `?here ping` or `?here tag`, and the bot will ping everyone from that list.
